pectĭnātim , adv. id.,
I.in the form of a comb, like the teeth of a comb: “cuniculatim, pectinatim divisa,” Plin. 9, 33, 52, § 103 : “digitis pectinatim inter se implexis,” id. 28, 6, 17, § 59 (cf.: “digitis inter se pectine junctis,” Ov. M. 9, 299 ): “serrati (dentes) pectinatim coëuntes,” Plin. 11, 37, 61, § 160 ; so, “pectinatim stipante se dentium serie,” id. 8, 25, 37, § 89 ; 8, 21, 30, § 75; Vitr 1, 5.
From A Latin Dictionary (Charlton T. Lewis, Charles Short, Oxford, Clarendon Press, 1879)
